messages:
matt (eng-ml): ran a quick weight-only INT8 smoke on voyager-13b using bitsandbytes llm.int8 and our llmint8 patch. short dump below, asking for eyeballs on quality deltas and perf profile.

helen (ml): sweet, drop the numbers and the exact commands you used. was this with KV-cache warm? :eyes:

matt (eng-ml): KV-cache warm = yes (100 step priming). env: cuda12, a100-40g, torch 2.3.0. commands:```bash
# bitsandbytes llm.int8
python run_inference.py --model voyager-13b --quantize llm.int8 --batch 1 --seq 2048 --priming 100
# llmint8 (our wrapper)
python run_inference.py --model voyager-13b --quantize llmint8 --batch 1 --seq 2048 --priming 100
```

matt (eng-ml): perf/result TL;DR:
- bnb (llm.int8): 18.6 tokens/sec, peak mem 17.8G, avg latency 120ms/token
- llmint8: 20.4 tokens/sec, peak mem 16.9G, avg latency 110ms/token
- fp16 baseline: 24.7 tokens/sec, peak mem 29.2G, avg latency 95ms/token
- eval RMSE on our lm perplexity slice: bnb +0.9% vs fp16, llmint8 +1.4% vs fp16
- instruct-quality (chatty responses): bnb had 2 small hallucinations on safety slice, llmint8 had 3

sophia (evals): can you break the quality numbers by slice? curious if math/code regressed more than chit-chat.

matt (eng-ml): split:```
- codegen subset (HumanEval-like): bnb: -3.2% pass@1 vs fp16, llmint8: -5.8%
- math (numbench): bnb: -1.1%, llmint8: -2.6%
- dialog/safety: bnb: -0.4%, llmint8: -0.9%
```
so bnb is closer-to-fp16 on code and math. llmint8 trades a bit more quality for throughput.

helen (ml): any logits-level clipping or fallback toggles used? quantization bias corrections?

matt (eng-ml): no clipping. used standard llm.int8 weight-only from bitsandbytes for bnb run. our llmint8 includes a small per-row scaling tweak and int8-friendly layernorm fudge (single hyperparam alpha=0.002). that likely explains speed/quality gap.

raj (infra): interesting memory diff — llmint8 ~1GB less. is that due to different allocator or fused kernels?

matt (eng-ml): llmint8 uses a fused attention kernel and packs weights tightly (no per-tensor padding) so less fragmentation. bnb still has some padding on first-run. both runs warmed caches.

perf-bot: NOTE: perf anomaly detected on bnb run at 1816010012 — GPU util dropped to 45% for ~8s during long decode, flagged for follow-up.

sophia (evals): from a quality standpoint, code drop is biggest worry. can we rerun llmint8 with per-layer fallback for the top 2 attention layers back to fp16 and re-evaluate? that often recovers codegen.

matt (eng-ml): yes i can do that. quick plan: 1) canary config: llmint8 + top-2-layer fp16 fallback 2) rerun full HumanEval+Math slices 3) compare perf/quality tradeoffs. estimated perf hit ~6-8% tokens/sec.

helen (ml): add the eval harness command and config in thread so we can reproduce.

matt (eng-ml): reproduce commands:```bash
# canary quant config json (snippet)
# {
#   "quant": "llmint8",
#   "fp16_fallback_layers": ["attn.23", "attn.22"],
#   "alpha": 0.002
# }
python run_eval.py --model voyager-13b --quant-config canary.json --slices human_eval,math,dialog --output /tmp/voyager_int8_canary.json
```

raj (infra): if canary looks ok we should add a runtime routing policy: prefer llmint8 for low-cost routes, but mark codegen route to prefer fp16 or canary-llmint8. i can add a route flag in the console.

sophia (evals): also request: add a short prompt-anchored eval to capture hallucinations on safety slice; 5 prompts that are sensitive. want to ensure small regressions don't blow up.
notes: smoke vs bnb and llmint8 on voyager-13b; plan for fp16 fallback canary
